description: Reference values of the non-compartmental analysis of the theophylline and the indomethacin dataset, transcribed from published results of Phoenix WinNonlin and PKNCA. Every number carries its source, its unit and the relative tolerance of the comparison. See tests/data/validation/README.md and docs/validation.md.

winnonlin-theoph-linear.title: Validation of Noncompartmental Analysis Performed by NonCompart R package

winnonlin-theoph-linear.settings: Theoph (n=12), extravascular, linear trapezoid ('down' of NonCompart), automatic (best fit) slope selection

winnonlin-indometh-linear-infusion.settings: Indometh (n=6), intravenous infusion of 0.25 h, linear trapezoid ('down' of NonCompart), automatic (best fit) slope selection; the report runs tblNCA(Indometh, "Subject", "time", "conc", dose=25, adm="Infusion", dur=0.25, concUnit="mg/L", R2ADJ=0.8)

theoph.dose_note: The dataset gives the dose as 'Dose' in mg/kg together with the body weight 'Wt' in kg; 'Dose' * 'Wt' is 267.8 mg for subject 9 and between 318.6 and 320.7 mg for the other eleven. The comparators analysed every subject against a flat 320 mg, so the validation does the same; only cl_f, vz_f, cmax_dn and auc_inf_dn depend on the dose.

indometh.dose_note: An intravenous bolus of 25 mg indomethacin. The concentrations are mcg/mL, which is the same quantity as the mg/L the comparators declared.

indometh-winnonlin-linear-infusion.note: linear trapezoid, the dataset analysed as a 0.25 h infusion

theoph-pknca.note: the per-subject numbers the PKNCA vignette prints for the subjects 1 and 6

theoph-pknca-partial.note: the vignette prints auclast of subject 1 for the automatic interval 0 to 24 h. PKNCA sums the trapezoids between the observations which fall inside an interval and does not interpolate at its end, so it truncates the interval to the last observation before 24 h, which is at 12.12 h for this subject. The number is compared through partial_auc over exactly that window.

theoph-pknca-summary.note: the summary of `pk.nca` over all twelve subjects the vignette prints: the geometric mean with the geometric coefficient of variation, the arithmetic mean and standard deviation of the half-life and the median with the range of tmax. The vignette prints two summaries, both over the twelve subjects: `summary(results_obj_automatic)`, whose 0 to Inf row carries cmax, tmax, half.life and aucinf.obs, and `summary(results_obj_manual)`, whose single 0 to Inf row carries auclast as well; auc_last_geomean and auc_last_geocv are taken from the second, since the auclast of the automatic summary belongs to its 0 to 24 h interval. PKNCA prints the coefficients of variation in percent, they are stored as fractions.
